EnemySizeBar.help.enemy_size_bar:
Enemy Size Bar
The enemies and items inside a level, like goombas or certain platforms, are stored as bytes in the ROM. This information is stored separately from the level objects, because multiple levels can share enemy data. Since enemy data is stored one after another, saving a level with more enemies, than it originally had, would overwrite another set of enemy data and probably cause the game to crash, if you would enter a level with broken enemy data while playing.
This bar shows, how much of the available space for enemies and items is currently taken up. It will turn red, when too many enemies have been placed.

FnsAsmLoadDialog.help.fns_asm_files:
A FNS file is a by-product of compiling a Rom file from assembly code.
It has all the labels used in the code and their positions as they would be in the NES's memory.
Some of these labels are used by the editor to find important data, like levels, palette colors, etc.
The editor, however, needs to know where the code these labels describe, is in the Rom file.
By default the editor ships with these addresses for the unaltered US SMB3 Rom, but if you have
made changes to the code, and things moved around, those addresses might not be valid anymore.
For that purpose, the editor needs the FNS file and your smb3.asm file as well, to generate the location
in the Rom for every label in the FNS file.

FoundryMainWindow.help.automatic_level_management:
Levels of the same type are stored in the same area of the ROM. If you add new objects to a Level, you might overwrite the Level, that comes right after it in memory.

Foundry can parse your ROM and find all Levels accessible to the player (!). That way, when you extend a Level, Foundry can automatically move the Levels, so that this doesn't happen and so that you can use as much memory as is available for that type of Level.

This can also be (de-)activated under 'Rom Settings' later.

JumpList.help.jump_list:
Jump List
Every level can designate another level to jump to, in case a pipe or a door is entered. This is done in the header, which can be edited with the Header Editor. While only one such level can be defined, where and how to enter that level can be defined multiple times with multiple jumps.
A jump is valid for one screen, a 16-block wide/high section of the level, depending on if the level is vertical or not, and all objects within that section, capable of handling a jump, will jump to the same position in the same way. To see where these jump zones are, enable the Jump Zone option in the View menu.

Tip: By having multiple jumps with different entry positions, you could make it look, like you are jumping to two different levels, when, in fact, you are jumping to two different sections of the same level.

LevelSizeBar.help.level_size_bar:
Level Size Bar
The objects inside a level, like platforms and item blocks, are stored as bytes in the ROM. Since levels are stored one after another, saving a level with more objects, than it originally had, would overwrite another level and probably cause the game to crash, if you would enter it, while playing.
This bar shows, how much of the available space for level objects is currently taken up. It will turn red, when too many level objects have been placed (or if the level objects would result in more bytes, than the level originally had).

LevelView.help.level_view:
Level View
This renders the level as it would appear in game plus additional information, that can be toggled in the View menu.
It supports selecting multiple objects, moving, copy/pasting and resizing them using the mouse or the usual keyboard shortcuts.
There are still occasional rendering errors, or small inconsistencies. If you find them, please report the kind of object (name or values in the SpinnerPanel) and the level or object set they appear in, in the discord and @Michael or on the github page under Help.

If all else fails, click the play button up top to see your level in game in seconds.

ObjectDropdown.help.object_dropdown:
Object Dropdown
Contains all objects and enemies/items, that can be placed in this type of level. Which are available depends on the object set, that is selected for this level.
You can search, by typing in the name, or simply select it from the list. After selecting an object, you can place it by clicking the middle mouse button anywhere in the level.

ObjectList.help.object_list:
Object List
This lists all the objects and enemies/items in the level. They appear in the order, that they are stored in the ROM as, which also decides which objects get drawn before/behind which.
Enemies/items are always listed last, since they are also stored separately from the level objects.

Note: While Jumps are technically level objects, they are omitted here, since they are listed in a separate list below.

ObjectToolBar.help.current_object:
Current Object
Shows the currently selected object and its name. It can be placed by clicking the middle mouse button anywhere in the level.

PaletteViewer.help.object_palettes:
Object Palettes
This shows the current palette group of the level, which can be changed in the level header editor.
By clicking on the individual colors, you can change them.

Note: The first color (the left most one) is always the same among all 4 palettes.

SpinnerPanel.help.spinner_panel:
Spinner Panel
The Spinner Panel gives raw byte access to objects for advanced users. The values are shown in hexadecimal notation.
Level objects and enemies/items are categorized using domains and indexes. Which domain an object is in, doesn't hold much information about the object, if at all.
As for the index, the only important information is, that all objects from 0x00 - 0x0F can not be resized. They have fixed dimensions, like the background bushes in Level 1-1.
All other objects have 16 different iterations, meaning 0x10 - 0x1F, for example, is one object, with 16 different sizes, going from smallest to largest. In what way these objects expand, depends on their particular expansion type.
Some '4-byte' objects can expand in a second way, since they have an additional byte holding that information. For example a platform, which can be sized vertically using the index and horizontally using the 4th byte.

TabbedToolBox.help.object_toolbox:
Object Toolbox
Contains all objects and enemies/items, that can be placed in this type of level. Which are available depends on the object set, that is selected for this level.
You can drag and drop objects into the level or click to select them. After selecting an object, you can place it by clicking the middle mouse button anywhere in the level.

Note: Some items, like blocks with items in them, are displayed as they appear in the ROM, mouse over them and check their names in the ToolTip, or use the object dropdown to find them directly.
